adapter: rsi6/environments/quadratic.py (class Quadratic, UBQP from the Biq Mac Library, sets beasley, gka a-e, be), manifest rsi6/environments/manifests/quadratic.json, data rsi6/data/quadratic/ (150 .sparse files, biqmaclib.tex, biqmaclib.html), in the package copy <scratch>/fresh/quadratic/repo
statement: The adapter reads and evaluates the Biq Mac quadratic instances correctly. It uses the 150 instances whose optimum the library publishes (bqp50/100/250, gka a-e and the eight be classes), and I found no defect in parsing or evaluation. My own parser and exact integer evaluator, written from biqmaclib.html and biqmaclib.tex, agree with it on all 150 reference values, all 150 matrices, all chance values and zero points, 360 complete answers (score difference 0.0), 3,150 candidate rows and 495 partial states. Its reading of the files (an entry i<j stands for q_ij and q_ji) is the right one, on three pieces of evidence: the library's full .mat files of gka3b and be200.3.7 equal that reading; under it a multi-start descent reaches the published value exactly on 14 small instances and never goes below it; under the other reading (each entry counted once) the descent goes below the published value on gka1b to gka4b. The problem object exposes only the instance (q_ii, q_ij, permuted by the seed). Nothing in it changes when the stored reference is altered, it is the same for training=True and False, and the score cannot be changed through it. The code contains no search, ranking or hint. Malformed answers score 0 and x = 0 scores 0, but the constant answer x = 1 scores above 0 on 85 of 150 instances (up to 0.44). The kernel's split gives 24 fresh instances (be200.3, be250, gka-b) and no twins. As the module says, 10 fresh files share long stretches of the generator's value stream with 7 training files, but their matrices agree position by position only at chance level. The main limitation is outside the adapter's code: computation on the exposed arrays is not metered. A one-flip descent that is charged no meter unit already scores 0.977 on the confirming half, and more such restarts lift the deciding half from about 0.82 to 0.96-0.99. So on this category neither reaching the threshold nor a gain within the metered budget shows learning unless it is compared with a plain-search control given the same CPU time. The anchor's descent figures for gka-b and the deciding half are 0.02 to 0.05 higher than an independent reproduction gives.
coverage:
Scripts are in <scratch>/fresh/quadratic/audit2 (aud_lib.py, aud1.py to aud12.py, aud5b.py, aud6b.py, aud6c.py). The scripts check1-4.py, mine.py and the folder dl/ were already there from an earlier session; I did not run them or use their results.

What each script checked:
- aud_lib.py: my own parser of the .tex tables (block by block, split at LaTeX row ends) and of the .sparse files, plus an exact evaluator using Python ints and Fractions.
- aud1: every manifest hash against the files on disk, files on disk against the manifest, the URLs, my parse of the tables against the adapter's values and n for all 150, every Q against my symmetric completion, the entry facts (no lower-triangle or duplicate entries), chance values and zero points (exact), the statements about 84/66 instances and 0.132, and the size rule.
- aud2: the view's public fields and state keys; every exposed array traced to the file under the decode permutation (150 instances x 2 seeds); monkeypatching best, zero and chance (pickle of the observable view and state); training True vs False; the reference and quantities derived from it searched in the exposed values; relabelling, including the per-instance seed computed with the kernel's crc32 formula, re-implemented rather than calling run._seed; decode with other dtypes and shapes.
- aud3: 360 answers over 12 instances (score, evaluate, decode, meter charges), candidates for assigned and unassigned variables against differences of partial_totals, totals after every assign against partial_totals and against my own partial value.
- aud4: 17 malformed or degenerate input forms on all 150 instances, against score() and the kernel's _valid; constant and trivial answers; random answers (400 per instance).
- aud5, aud5b, aud12: the split and halves, one layout, twins and near-duplicates, and the bin-packing six-value rule.
- aud6, aud6b, aud6c: the anchor's descent figures, over 19 runs of 30 descents per fresh instance; local minima confirmed with the adapter's own candidates().
- aud7: which reading of the files fits the published values.
- aud8: 5 files fetched again plus 2 .mat files and the beasley folder listing (curl -A research-data-check/1.0, parsed as bytes or text only), and the terms on the live page.
- aud9: further numerical statements of the module (gka-b chance values, stream claims, orientation figures; all approximately reproduced).
- aud10: positional patterns in file order and after relabelling (none).
- aud11: edge cases, and isolation of the scoring matrix from the problem object.

rsi6.kernel.run was imported only for split, halves, layout and _valid, with rsi6.learner replaced in sys.modules by an empty stub, so no learner module was imported. No learner was built or run. test_kernel.py was not run because it imports the learner; I re-implemented its checks that do not involve the learner. Bytecode writing was disabled, and no file under the repo copy changed (find -newer showed none).

Not checked:
- Optimality of the published values (by instruction).
- The other 118 .mat files.
- The builder's statement that the threshold was fixed before any answer was scored (the copy holds no ledger).
- The claim "not redistributed by this package" (the copy is not under version control).
- The module's up/down-run claims for gka pairs and for the 13 bqp50/bqp100 pairs.

Out of scope and not findings: score() accepts a Python list of 0/1, while the kernel's _valid refuses lists before scoring. The kernel's generic AssignProblem.evaluate casts a float answer to int64 before checking it (a learner-side tool, not the scoring path).

Compute: my first run of aud1.py ran about 2 CPU-minutes before I stopped it, which exceeds the 60-CPU-second limit per command. The cause was an O(m^2) bug in my own entry check. Every later command ran under ulimit -t 60 and took at most about 10 CPU-seconds. The total was about 2.7 CPU-minutes, with one Python process at a time.
evaluator_agreement:
Reference values: all 150 values I parsed from the pinned biqmaclib.tex equal env.reference(). I found 165 table rows: 150 with a value and 15 bounds (bqp500-1..10, gka1f..5f). No instance-like token in a table row was skipped. The adapter's instance set is exactly the 150 instances with a value. n agrees with the table for all 150.

Matrices: Q equals my symmetric completion of the .sparse list for all 150. No file has a lower-triangle or duplicate entry.

Chance values and zero points: equal my exact Fractions for all 150. A Monte Carlo check (be150.8.3, 20,000 answers) gives -13.05 +- 17.79 against the closed form -38.50, which is consistent.

Complete answers: 360 random answers over 12 instances. Adapter score() against my exact score: largest difference 0.0. problem.evaluate() totals against my integer x'Qx: all equal. decode(answer in problem labels) returns my file-label answer exactly, with the dtype kept. Meter charges are n per evaluate, 2 per candidate variable and 1 per assign.

Partial evaluation: 3,150 candidate rows, with variables assigned to 0, assigned to 1 and unassigned, all equal the difference of partial_totals. totals() after every assign (36 full constructions) equals partial_totals, and 495 partial states equal my own value of the terms whose variables are all assigned. The fast _rows equals the default AssignProblem._rows over all variables of a half-assigned gka2b state.

Reading of the files: the library's .mat files of gka3b and be200.3.7, fetched again, equal the symmetric completion of the .sparse files and not the upper triangle alone. With 200 starts of my own one-flip descent, the symmetric reading reaches the published value exactly on all 14 small instances tried and never goes below it. The each-entry-once reading goes below the published value on gka1b (-154 against -133), gka2b (-146 against -121), gka3b (-134 against -118) and gka4b (-148 against -129).

The source publishes values only, no solution vectors. Attainment was also seen on 7 of the 24 fresh instances with the best of 30 descents.
exposed:
- n_vars = n: the first token of the .sparse file, equal to the table's n.
- n_opts = 2 (x_i = 0 or 1, from the answer form); n_groups = 1, hard = [False], detail = [False]: the single soft total x'Qx; the specification has no constraint.
- ordered = False; capacity, domain, start_answer and start_totals are None.
- var_attr (n x 1): q_ii, the file's entry (i,i), 0 where the file lists none.
- var_var[0] (n x n): q_ij for i != j, the file's entry (min(i,j), max(i,j)); symmetric, zero diagonal.
- Both var_attr and var_var have rows and columns permuted by the seed's permutation. I verified both against the file for all 150 instances under 2 seeds.
- opt_attr is (2 x 0); opt_opt, var_opt and occ_attr are empty.
- Through calls: start, candidates (the exact change of x'Qx for each variable and option, including the flip change of an assigned variable), assign, totals (the partial x'Qx over the terms whose variables are all assigned) and evaluate. All are computed from Q alone.
- Hidden behind the view: the problem object's extra attribute diag (equal to var_attr) and the state's field, the sum of q_vj over the variables set to 1. Neither depends on the reference.

Nothing is derived from the reference, and no heuristic attribute is exposed. One design decision shapes the difficulty: the whole of Q is exposed as plain arrays, so any search on them is free of the meter, and plain descent nearly solves these instances (finding 1). The zero point min(chance, 0) narrows the scale to [0, optimum] on 66 instances, among them every gka-b instance; there local minima score anywhere from 0.38 to 1.0.

findings.title: Neither the threshold nor a gain within the metered budget separates learning from unmetered search; the anchor's remedy is incomplete
findings.problem: The meter charges only start, candidates, assign and evaluate (problem.py lines 113, 132, 144, 169). var_attr and var_var hold all of Q, so search on them is free. As the module says, a plain procedure passes the threshold 0.97 without a metered call. But the anchor's remedy, 'Only the gain over the untrained answer can be evidence here', does not hold either. More unmetered restarts raise the score with nothing learned, inside the same metered budget. An acquired capability that amounts to searching longer on the exposed arrays would therefore count as a gain, and a reader following the anchor would misread it as learning.
findings.evidence: aud6.py runs the steepest one-flip descent on the view's arrays with Meter(0.0) and asserts P.meter.used == 0; the assertion passed. Seeds 99, 5 and 2026 give: confirming half (be200.3) one descent 0.977-0.978, best of 10 0.994-0.995, best of 30 0.997-0.999; deciding half (be250, gka-b) one descent 0.810-0.826, best of 10 0.948-0.969, best of 30 0.982-0.991. aud6b.py, 16 further runs: deciding one descent 0.807-0.828, best of 10 0.944-0.972. Going from 1 to 10 unmetered descents is thus a 'gain' of about 0.12-0.15 on the deciding half and 0.017 on the confirming half, and the confirming half passes 0.97 with a single descent.
findings.fix: In quadratic.py, replace the last sentence of the anchor ('Only the gain over the untrained answer can be evidence here') and the corresponding module paragraph (lines 91-95 and 115-121) with: 'Neither reaching the threshold nor a gain within the metered budget is evidence here: computation on var_attr and var_var is not metered, so more search on them raises the score without anything learned; a gain counts only when the acquired and the untrained answers were produced with equal CPU time, or against a plain one-flip-descent control given the same CPU time.' The registration of any test that uses quadratic must state and enforce that equal-CPU control, and must not count a threshold crossing on quadratic as an acquired capability. If CPU cannot be controlled, quadratic must not be used for capability claims. The only alternative inside the adapter is to stop exposing var_attr and var_var, so that Q reaches the learner only through metered calls.

findings.title: The anchor's and the module's descent figures for gka-b and the deciding half are not reproduced
findings.problem: The module's table (lines 102-107) and the anchor state: one descent 0.841 on the deciding half (gka-b 0.750); best of 3, 10 and 30 0.929, 0.978 and 0.993; all 24 fresh 0.892, 0.951, 0.984 and 0.995; 'the best of 10 descents reaches it on both halves'; 'the best of 10 0.975 to 0.982 on the deciding half in each of its 3 blocks'. An independent implementation of the stated procedure gives lower figures on gka-b, the deciding half and all 24. The procedure is the steepest one-flip descent from uniform random answers, 30 runs per fresh instance, scored by the adapter, with local minima confirmed by the adapter's own candidates(). The confirming-half and be250 figures are reproduced.
findings.evidence: From aud6.py and aud6b.py: 19 runs, 11 breaking ties by first index and 8 at random. Deciding one descent 0.807-0.828 (stated 0.841). gka-b one descent 0.692-0.727 (stated 0.750). Deciding best of 10 0.944-0.972, at 0.97 or above in only 4 of 19 runs (stated 0.978). Deciding best-of-10 blocks 0.930-0.962 (stated 0.975-0.982). Deciding best of 30 0.982-0.991 (stated 0.993). All 24: one descent 0.873-0.883 and best of 3 0.928-0.938 (stated 0.892 and 0.951). Confirming half 0.977-0.978, best of 3 0.988-0.989, as stated. aud6c.py: 0 of 120 end points were not one-flip local minima.
findings.fix: Re-measure with a pinned seed and give the spread over seeds, or replace the deciding-half, gka-b and all-24 figures with the reproduced ranges. Replace 'the best of 10 descents reaches it on both halves' with 'the best of 30 descents reaches it on both halves (deciding half 0.982 to 0.991)'. Correct the numbers in the anchor string the same way.

findings.title: The constant answer x = 1 scores above 0 on 85 of 150 instances; the zero-point text is silent on it
findings.problem: The module calls the zero point 'the smaller of two values that need no work' and shows that x = 0 scores 0 everywhere. The other constant answer, x = 1, needs no work either, yet it scores above 0 on 85 instances, up to 0.44. That a constant answer can earn part of the scale is not stated anywhere.
findings.evidence: aud4.py: all1 mean 0.082, max 0.440, above 0 on 85 of 150 instances; highest cases gka5c 0.440, bqp50-6 0.407, bqp100-3 0.404 (all0 is 0 everywhere). aud5.py: on the deciding half mean 0.022, max 0.104, above 0 on 5 of 15; on the confirming half mean 0.018, max 0.123, above 0 on 3 of 9. Random answers: 0.0299 over the 150 and 0.0141 over the 24 fresh, as stated.
findings.fix: Add these figures to the zero-point paragraph of the module (lines 70-85). If both constant answers are to score 0 by construction, set zero = min(chance, 0, Q.sum()) (the value of x = 1) in __init__, and recompute the bound 'a score s is a value of s to s + c(1 - s) of the optimum' with the new largest zero/optimum ratio.

findings.title: The split and the halves fail the stream rule the bin-packing adapter is held to (disclosed and verified; not a near-duplicate)
findings.problem: The be files of one generator seed share the library generator's stream of values. 10 of the 24 fresh files share long runs of listed values with 7 training files, and 6 deciding files with 6 confirming files. test_binpacking_training_and_fresh_share_no_stretch would refuse such a split. The module states this accurately and leaves the decision to the registration. My measurements show the matrices are not related position by position, so I see no exploitable leak, but no decision on consistency with the project's rule has been recorded.
findings.evidence: aud12.py: 12 training x fresh pairs (10 fresh files) share 1,174-4,781 runs of six listed values; 6 deciding x confirming pairs share 1,726-1,871. aud5.py: the k-th listed value is equal for 0.414-0.974 (training x fresh) and 0.898-0.939 (halves) of k < 2000, as stated; there are no permutation twins and at most 4% equal diagonal entries. aud5b.py: over pairs with at least 200 common nonzero positions, equal values are at most 0.02 and |corr| at most 0.20 (chance level). aud9.py: be200.3.6 lies within be200.8.6 for 0.988 of its nonzero positions; be200.8.6 has density 0.788.
findings.fix: The registration of any test using quadratic must record whether the six-value stream rule applies. If it does, group the be files by generator seed (all be classes of seed k in one group) or remove from the fresh side the be files whose seed number is used in training, and keep be250.k and be200.3.k in one half. If it does not, the registration must state that the shared streams were measured and judged harmless (values at common positions agree at chance level).
